_note: Verified naval plate set. Every plate below was opened individually at full resolution and looked at; every crop rect was rendered with ffmpeg and looked at. crop is [x,y,w,h] as fractions of the SOURCE image. both:true = a UI trim applied to BOTH images. both:false = a reframe applied to the PLATE ONLY, and the scenario camera must be authored to match that framing. Every rect is 16:9 (+/-0.2%) in real pixels so compare.mjs's fit() does not crop it a second time — see REVIEW.md B4.
_verified: 2026-08-05, second pass. The first pass was triaged from 4x4 contact sheets at 440px/tile and was wrong: 4 of its 20 'clean' plates carried a full HUD, 2 were mislabelled, 2 carried copyright watermarks.
_sheet: compare.mjs fit() = scale to fill 900x506 then centre-crop. Target aspect 1.77866.

236390_05.use: Yamato-class battleship bow-on at speed, sheets of spray tearing off the forecastle, funnel smoke, blue sky with cumulus. Bow-wave and spray VFX, painted-steel hull material.

236390_09.use: Battleship firing a full main-battery broadside, elevated 3/4 rear. Muzzle bloom, brown propellant smoke rolling downwind, wake. The best clean naval-gunnery plate on the board.

236390_14.use: French battleship steaming under low sun, floatplane overhead, distant coast, funnel smoke. Open-ocean colour grade and horizon haze.
236390_14.why_crop: A faint two-line watermark sits in the bottom-left corner at roughly x 14-36, y 977-990. The trim removes the left 4% and bottom 4%; applied to BOTH images so the trim itself cannot become the tell. Verified by rendering the trimmed bottom-left corner at 2x contrast: gone.
236390_14.caveat: The plate has a hero warship. A shipless ocean render scored against it loses Composition. C1's sea_noon scenario should carry at least one distant silhouetted hull.

242050_01.use: Storm at sea in heavy rain: an enemy man-o'-war firing a full broadside with round shot visibly mid-flight over a big rolling swell. The only plate on the board with projectiles in the air.

494840_09.use: Chart table under a single warm lamp, navigator plotting, dark room falling off to black. The lamp-on-a-lit-surface lighting model for the planning table.

494840_10.use: Night sea under a black sky: a torpedoed freighter burning on the horizon, its fire the only light source, rimming the swell orange all the way to camera.
494840_10.why_crop: No UI anywhere in this frame — the crop is a pure reframe. The uncropped shot is dominated by a surfaced U-boat filling the lower half, which an ocean/sky/light component has nothing to answer with. The rect is 770x433 at (1150,0) of a 1920x1080 source: it drops the submarine entirely and keeps sky, horizon, the burning hulk and the fire-lit water. One faint rigging line crosses the bottom-left corner. Verified by rendering. The scenario camera must be authored to this framing.
494840_10.caveat: Even cropped there is a distant burning ship. Put one on the horizon in the scenario or the comparison is not like for like. No press pack anywhere contains an empty night ocean.

494840_11.use: Dark painted-steel interior, red valve accents, small practical lights, grimy metal. Interior material read.

494840_13.use: Cutaway of the submarine's compartments under practical lighting. Secondary interior material reference. The black bands top and bottom are the game's cutaway framing, not letterbox.

1172620_00.use: Five galleons in line under a bright blue sky on teal tropical water. Fleet silhouette spacing and daylight water. Stylised — read it for composition and light, not for water detail.

1172620_02.use: Torch-lit stone vault with a table and gold. Warm firelight on a horizontal surface in a dark room. Secondary to 494840_09.

1172620_07.use: Deck-level view down a galleon's gun deck as the broadside fires. Muzzle bloom and lit smoke cards doing all the work; the cheap-VFX-done-well target.

1172620_12.use: Close muzzle flash at a cannon's mouth: core bloom, cordite puff, ember sparks, painted wood lit by the flash.
1172620_12.why_crop: The uncropped frame carries two pieces of readable text: the transom name 'THE UNBROKEN BOND' (approx x 547-728, y 483-527) and an Emissary banner reading 'SILVER SWO... VI' (approx x 1371-1700, y 421-524). Either identifies the game in one search. The rect is the bottom-left quadrant, 960x540 at (0,540), which excludes both. Verified by rendering.

1272010_00.use: WW2 destroyer making smoke in a daylight convoy, escorts and a burning ship strung along the horizon. Realistic fleet-scale composition and haze.
1272010_00.why_crop: Destroyer's HUD is on in every press shot: left menu (to x 230), an icon strip at x 0-290 y 360-440, three left dials (x 0-190), a top bearing tape (y to 110), a right binocular button (x 1845+), a bottom-centre bearing bar (y 1035+) and a chat log (x 1270+, y 915+). The rect 1352x760 at (300,130) is the largest 16:9 box that clears all of them. Verified: left edge, bottom edge and full frame each rendered and inspected. An earlier rect starting at x=250 leaked the amber icon strip.

1272010_01.use: Burning freighters at dusk in rain: fire columns on the waterline, smoke going up into the murk, orange firelight rippling across a dark sea.
1272010_01.why_crop: Same always-on HUD as 1272010_00, same rect. The rain at the top and the orange-lit water at the bottom — the two things the plate is for — are both inside it. Verified by rendering.

1272010_02.use: Red-lit night bridge: a row of bright portholes showing a grey sea and burning ships outside, brass and glass instruments in near-black, a glowing engine telegraph. The interior/exterior exposure problem (BUILD_PLAN 7.1) in one frame.
1272010_02.why_crop: 1600x900 at (300,0). Clears the left menu, the icon strip, the left dials and the chat log. The lettering that survives (TARGET BEARING, STOP/BACK/FULL) is in-world instrument art, not overlay UI. Verified by rendering.

1272010_04.use: DRT plotting table seen from above: amber-lit paper, a mechanical bearing plotter, a parallel rule, pencilled fixes with times against them. The direct ancestor of our peg grid.
1272010_04.why_crop: 1400x787 at (300,40). Clears the left menu and icon strip, the right tool palette (x 1855+), the bottom tab bar (RADAR/DRT/OSC/...) at y 1035+ and the chat log. Verified by rendering.

1272010_05.use: Torpedoed freighter at blue hour: a tall smoke column, tracer arcs, our own foredeck in the near foreground, convoy silhouettes on the horizon. Alternate night-sea / hit plate.
1272010_05.why_crop: Same always-on HUD, same rect as 1272010_00. Verified by rendering.

1272010_06.use: A hit seen from our own bow rail: a freighter burning at close range, white-hot core, black smoke column, water lit orange all the way to the rail.
1272010_06.why_crop: Same always-on HUD, same rect as 1272010_00. Verified by rendering.

552990_08.use: Pure open-ocean sunset: banded cloud, a low sun, a specular glitter path running down the water to camera. No ships, no land, no VFX — the only shipless sky-and-water grade plate on the board, which makes it the right target for an ocean/sky/light component.
552990_08.why_crop: 590x332 at (1310,150). Every other region of this frame holds HUD: the top-right ribbon block, range labels, a DETECTED marker at (1180-1245, 300-345), a 0.8 km marker at (1255-1300, 420-490), a Target-hits panel, the bottom-left ship panel, the consumables bar and the minimap. This rect is the largest 16:9 box that clears all of them. Verified by rendering and inspecting.
552990_08.caveat: 590px wide, so it upscales 1.53x to the 900px sheet cell and will read soft. Do not read the Finish criterion off this plate.

1489630_00.use: Dark red-lit bridge built around a glowing holographic plot table, instrument screens around the walls, a window band forward. Layout and emissive-table treatment.
1489630_00.caveat: Source is 1920x1017 (1.888), not 16:9, so fit() centre-crops about 3% off each side — dark bulkhead only. Carrier Command 2's art outside these dark bridge shots is flat-shaded low-poly and would score badly; this plate is a layout and emissive reference, not a materials bar.

1489630_15.use: The same bridge at night with the carrier's lit flight deck visible through the window — a bright exterior seen from a dark interior. Same 1920x1017 caveat as 1489630_00.

2853730_08.use: Storm-grey sea, two ships shelling a fort: one tall white splash column standing in mid-frame, incendiary tracer arcs overhead, a bright impact on the fort wall. The only clean shell-splash column on the board.
2853730_08.caveat: The ordnance is fantasy (fire arrows, rockets), so read the splash column, the storm water and the sky — not the projectile VFX.

shot_notes.sea_dusk: 552990_08's rect is sky and water and nothing else, which is exactly what an ocean/sky/light component renders. It is small (590px) and will read soft; score grade, not sharpness.
shot_notes.sea_night: 494840_10 carries a reframe (both:false) even though it has no UI — the uncropped shot is dominated by a submarine the renderer will not have. Even cropped it has a distant burning hulk, so the scenario should place one on the horizon or the comparison is not like for like. No press pack anywhere contains an empty night ocean.
shot_notes.sea_noon: 236390_14 has a hero battleship. Put one distant silhouetted hull in the scenario or accept a Composition loss.
shot_notes.fleet_wide: 1272010_00 (realistic WW2 convoy, cropped) is the honest match for warships spread across an ocean. 1172620_00 is the stylised alternative if the game's grade lands closer to Sea of Thieves.
shot_notes.guns_fire: 1172620_07 is the wide gun-deck version; 1172620_12 (cropped) is the close muzzle-flash version. Pick one and keep it fixed across rounds.
shot_notes.shell_flight: 242050_01 is the only plate here with projectiles visibly in the air. It is a storm scene with a sailing ship, so it is a VFX/atmosphere target, not a framing target.
shot_notes.window_out: Scored as a pair. @0.0 against 1272010_02 (dark bridge, bright portholes) and @1.0 against 236390_14 (bright open sea). Both are daylight-outside, so the pair is internally consistent.
shot_notes.match_cut: No plate. No shipped game does the peg-becomes-shell cut. Score on the rubric alone per BUILD_PLAN 4.3.
shot_notes.GAPS: No defensible plate exists for a pure empty ocean at any time of day, for a shell in flight from a rifled naval gun, or for a bridge-to-ocean transition. Every candidate for those is listed above with the mismatch stated. Do not substitute a plate that does not match the shot — record the gap instead.
